title: Phase 3a and 3b update of the gastric cancer module, EORTC QLQ-STO22
official: Phase 3a and 3b update of the gastric cancer module, European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC) Quality of Life Questionnaire (QLQ) Stomach Cancer 22 items (STO22)
summary:
Background and study aims 
Although the EORTC QLQ-STO22 (QLQ-STO22) is one of the most widely used measures of quality of life for people with stomach (gastric) cancer, it needs to be updated to capture issues related to new and diverse treatment approaches which have been licenced since the beginning of the century when the development of the original QLQ-STO22 started. Updating the QLQ-STO22 will also provide the opportunity to consider the experiences and perspectives of patients and healthcare professionals (HCPs) from countries which were not included in the original development of the QLQ-STO22, and in particular those from East Asia.
The first phase of the update, which identified whether an update was needed, has been completed. It involved collecting and reviewing information on stomach cancer from a systematic review and interviews with 18 HCPs and 104 patients across 10 countries, including four from East Asia and three non-European countries. 
The systematic review and interviews with HCPs and patients found no evidence that culturally specific adaptations to the QLQ-STO22 were needed. However, the systematic review and interviews found some quality of life issues were missing including flatulence, eating small amounts and peripheral neuropathy symptoms. In the second phase of the update, the EORTC quality of life group (QLG) recommended removing two non-specific questions (i.e., thinking about illness and worry about the future). Also, the translation team recommended adaptations to the wording of seven items (from ‘Did you…?’ To ‘Have you…?’). 
An updated version of the QLQ-STO22 including five additional questions (covering the three missing issues) and linguistic changes to the seven questions needs to be pilot tested with a larger group of patients with stomach cancer including those from East Asia. This Phase 3 involves testing the updated QLQ-STO22 for its relevance to patients with stomach cancer, to identify and solve potential problems in its administration, and identify missing or redundant issues. The scale structure of the provisional measure will also be explored. The outcome of this work will be an updated measure of quality of life issues of specific relevance to patients with stomach cancer across different cultures and treated with current protocols.

Who can participate? 
People aged at least 18 years of age with stomach cancer stages 1-4, who can understand, speak and read English (or Welsh for patients recruited in Wales), and who are able to give informed consent. 

What does the study involve? 
When evaluating the impact of an illness, such as cancer and its treatments, one of the most important areas to consider is the effect on people’s quality of life quality of life. Quality of life can be affected in a number of ways by cancer and its treatment, and different patients may have different experiences. We have created an updated version of a quality of life questionnaire used specifically for stomach cancer, known as the EORTC QLQ-STO22. We need to test the updated version of our questionnaire and would like you to complete it and comment on it. We would like to speak to people with stomach cancer to find out all the different ways the effects of stomach cancer and its treatment affect people’s lives and also to find the best way to measure the effects of stomach cancer on people’s lives and whether the updated version of the questionnaire is suitable.
To take part we will ask patients to read a participant information sheet and ask any questions about participating to their friends, healthcare team or the research team. If they decide to take part patients will be asked to give informed consent and then answer some questions about themselves. Patients will be asked to complete some questionnaires, with questions asking about issues relating to their quality of life, and how much they experience each of the issues. The researcher will then ask some questions about the questionnaires; this is important as we are interested in whether the patients have any suggestions for questions, such as whether any should be removed, re-worded, if any questions are missing or not understandable. 
The study involves a one-off discussion with a researcher. There will be no follow ups and is likely to take up to 20 minutes, but no longer than 1 hour.  

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating? 
It is hoped that the information provided to us by patients will help make sure we are measuring what matters most to people with stomach cancer.

Where is the study run from? 
University of Southampton (UK)

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for? 
October 2026 to May 2029

Who is funding the study? 
European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC) (UK)

Who is the main contact? 
Amy Din (study coordinator), A.E.Din@soton.ac.uk

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Adults (aged ≥18 years)
2. Histologically confirmed gastric adenocarcinoma with an epicentre located within 2 cm from the gastroesophageal junction
3. Stages I–IV
4. On treatment (chemotherapy, radiotherapy, targeted or immunotherapy or surgery) or within 1 year of finishing treatment or receiving supportive or palliative care
5. Ability to provide informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
1. Unable to speak the native language of the recruiting centre (i.e., for UK sites this will be either English or Welsh) 
2. Inability to complete questionnaires due to language or cognitive limitations. 
3. Participated in Phase 1 (or Phase 3a for patients approached for Phase 3b) of the QLQ-STO22 update
4. Patients with a concurrent malignancy 
5. Cancer survivors defined as people who have completed treatment with curative intent more than 1 year ago and are now cancer free
6. Patients enrolled in other quality of life studies which might affect the results of the current study, e.g., the update of the EORTC oesophageal cancer - QLQ OES18 and QLQ OG25
7. Patients who have not started active treatment yet
